title: Matlab & Python demonstration on Simplified Bias and Gravity Compensation for Wrist-Mounted F/T sensor
creator: Dayuan (GitHub leledeyuan00, Tohoku University Smart Robots Design Lab)
access: Public GitHub, free without login. No LICENSE file at this commit; GitHub repository license field null. Link to the original measurements; only independent derived statistics and a reader are included here.
hardware: README identifies an ATI Axis-80 EtherCAT sensor and ROS2. The authors describe the static stand as approximately 35 hours. Seven columns encode time in seconds, three forces and three moments.
observed: The 130,511 times strictly increase and span 130,510.076489 s (36.252799 h). The input describes a stationary sensor. It does not include temperature, a traceable unloaded zero or an external reference wrench.

Between the first and last 600 samples, the mean Fz changes +0.635238617 N and mean Mz changes +0.001255193 Nm. The hourly table supports a check of whether drift is linear or persists through the whole stand.

The 7-pose and 100-pose files specify position/quaternion and measured wrench expressed in the robot base frame. The pinned code estimates base gravity, sensor-fixed force offsets, an axial center-of-mass distance, and sensor-fixed moment offsets. Fitting seven samples reproduces gravity_result.txt to its printed precision.

The seven-pose fit has RMS vector residuals 0.257968 N and 0.004969 Nm on the same file. Applying that unchanged fit to the hundred-pose measurements gives 4.504126 N and 0.203784 Nm. Separately refitting the hundred-pose file gives 0.497332 N and 0.006096 Nm on that file.
GP2025-07-22-22-06-02.txt separately contains 1,756 finite 11-column samples of time, six-axis wrench and quaternion; its extra pose channels are absent from the long static trace.
limitations: The static sensor may carry preload or tool weight. Drift is a change in recorded signal. Temperature causation and absolute sensor bias cannot be identified without additional reference channels.

The acquisition setup, payload, retaring and other changes between the two pose collections are unspecified. Cross-file residuals quantify transfer at the recorded settings; they do not identify the cause of the change.
A related publication is Chen et al. DOI 10.1109/ROBIO66223.2025.11376212. The GitHub README does not explicitly identify the paper or claim that every file is a manuscript experiment.
